successCriteria.description: IEmployeeService interface declares exactly the operations findById, findByManagerId, isActive, and getManagerId, and EmployeeService implements that interface.
EmployeeService delegates all data access to an injected IEmployeeRepository (findById / findByManagerId) and never imports or touches the pg pool or shared/db/connection directly.
isActive returns true if and only if the resolved employee's employmentStatus equals EmploymentStatus.ACTIVE; it returns false for a non-existent employee id.
getManagerId returns the managerId field of the resolved Employee (string | null), including null for a top-level employee and null when the employee id is not found.
ILeavePolicyService interface declares exactly findByLeaveType, getEntitlement, requiresManagerApproval, and getMinimumNoticeDays, and LeavePolicyService implements that interface.
LeavePolicyService delegates all data access to an injected ILeavePolicyRepository and never imports or touches the pg pool or shared/db/connection directly.

getEntitlement, requiresManagerApproval, and getMinimumNoticeDays resolve the policy by filtering findByLeaveType results to isActive === true and taking the first match; when no active policy exists they return a typed null/absent result without throwing.
Unit tests mock the injected repository interface via jest.fn() and cover the found, not-found, active-policy-filtering, and null-manager cases; `npm run build` (tsc --noEmit) and jest both pass.

constraints: Strict TypeScript: no implicit any, strict null checks, and the no-any rule (use unknown with type guards instead of any) — must pass `npm run build` (tsc --noEmit).
GP-001 Repository pattern: services must inject repository interfaces (IEmployeeRepository, ILeavePolicyRepository) and never query the database or import the pg pool / shared/db/connection directly.

Service interface methods must omit PoolClient parameters — these services are thin read-only lookup wrappers, not transaction orchestrators; the repository methods retain PoolClient for higher-level callers.

New files must follow the module convention: src/modules/<name>/<name>.service.interface.ts for the interface and <name>.service.ts for the implementation; tests mirror tests/unit/modules/<name>/<name>.service.test.ts.

No circular dependencies: Employee and LeavePolicy services depend only on their own module's model/repository and SharedTypes, matching the reconciled dependency map (Employee → SharedTypes, LeavePolicy → SharedTypes).
outOfScope: LeaveBalanceService, LeaveRequestService, controller, routes, and app wiring (Phases 8–10) — not created in this phase.
Module index.ts barrel files for employee and leave-policy — not in the 6-file scope of this phase (only status/uptime have barrels today).

Any write/mutation operations (create/update/delete) on employees or leave policies — these services are read-only lookups; no audit records are required (GP-002 applies only to state-changing operations).
RBAC enforcement / auth middleware (GP-005) — these services have no API surface; RBAC is enforced at the route layer in Phase 10.
HR escalation logic for null managerId (business rule 3 escalation to hr_admin) — that orchestration belongs to the LeaveRequestService in Phase 9; getManagerId only returns the raw managerId.

entityInvariants.invariant: An employee's active eligibility is determined solely by employmentStatus === EmploymentStatus.ACTIVE; INACTIVE and TERMINATED employees are not active. The service must not infer active status from any other field (e.g. terminationDate, deletedAt).

managerId is the authoritative approval-routing reference: it is either a string referencing another employee's id or null (top-level / no manager). The service exposes it verbatim without defaulting or synthesizing a value.

Only policies with isActive === true are considered the governing policy for a leave type; inactive policies returned by the repository must be filtered out before resolving entitlement, approval requirement, or notice days.
minimumNoticeDays is nullable (number | null); a null value means no advance-notice constraint applies. The service must preserve null rather than coercing it to 0 or throwing.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns the Employee or null when not found; must not throw on a missing id. Delegates to IEmployeeRepository.findById without a PoolClient.
Returns the array of direct-report Employees (possibly empty) for the given manager id; delegates to IEmployeeRepository.findByManagerId without a PoolClient.
Returns a boolean: true iff the resolved employee's employmentStatus === EmploymentStatus.ACTIVE; false when the employee is not found or is INACTIVE/TERMINATED. Must not throw on a missing id.
Returns the managerId (string | null) of the resolved employee, or null when the employee is not found. Must not throw on a missing id.
Returns the array of LeavePolicy entries for the given LeaveType (delegates to ILeavePolicyRepository.findByLeaveType without a PoolClient); may be empty.
Resolves the active policy for the leave type and returns its entitlementDays, or a typed null/absent result when no active policy exists; must not throw on missing policy.
Resolves the active policy for the leave type and returns its requiresManagerApproval boolean, or a typed null/absent result when no active policy exists; must not throw on missing policy.

Resolves the active policy for the leave type and returns its minimumNoticeDays (number | null), or a typed null/absent result when no active policy exists; must not throw on missing policy and must preserve a null minimumNoticeDays.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: EmployeeService must consume the Employee entity shape exactly as defined (employmentStatus: EmploymentStatus, managerId: string | null) — do not redefine or widen the Employee type.
EmployeeService must call only the findById and findByManagerId signatures declared on IEmployeeRepository (with optional PoolClient omitted); it must not depend on findAll/create/update/softDelete.

LeavePolicyService must consume the LeavePolicy entity shape exactly as defined (entitlementDays: number, requiresManagerApproval: boolean, minimumNoticeDays: number | null, isActive: boolean) — do not redefine or widen the LeavePolicy type.
LeavePolicyService must call only the findByLeaveType signature declared on ILeavePolicyRepository (with optional PoolClient omitted); it must not depend on findById or findAllActive.
isActive must compare against EmploymentStatus.ACTIVE from the shared enum, not a hardcoded string literal, to stay aligned with the canonical enum values.
Service interface + implementation file naming and the `implements` pattern must match the established convention in the status and uptime modules.

Service unit tests must follow the existing repository test conventions: jest.mock of the dependency, jest.fn() mocks reset in beforeEach, makeX(overrides) factory helpers, describe/it structure, and relative import paths.

integrationPoints.why: EmployeeService injects this repository interface to resolve employees by id and by manager id; it is the sole data-access dependency for the employee service.
LeavePolicyService injects this repository interface to look up policies by leave type; it is the sole data-access dependency for the leave-policy service.
isActive compares against EmploymentStatus.ACTIVE; findByLeaveType/getEntitlement/etc. accept a LeaveType argument; both enums are imported from the shared types module.

IEmployeeService (manager resolution, active-status gate) and ILeavePolicyService (entitlement, approval requirement, minimum notice) are consumed by the future LeaveRequestService orchestrator per the reconciled dependency map (LeaveRequest → Employee, LeavePolicy).
